title: Vector-bundle Thom isomorphism
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $\pi:E\to B$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $r$ with zero
section $z$. The morphism
$\tau_E:\Lambda_B\to R\pi_!\Lambda_E(r)[2r]$ of
[def-pur-vector-bundle-thom-class] is an isomorphism, compatible
with base change and with direct sums of vector bundles. Its inverse
is the *vector-bundle trace*

$$
\operatorname{tr}_\pi:R\pi_!\Lambda_E(r)[2r]\longrightarrow\Lambda_B.
$$

proof.text: Work at the arbitrary finite level $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, of [def-pur-conventions], and put $Q_E=A_E(r)[2r]$. The finite twists in [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] are locally constant finite rank-one coefficient sheaves: [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] supplies this for the prescribed pro-etale $A(1)$, and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] supplies all tensor powers, duals and their pullback identifications on the etale representatives. The inverse-limit reduction identity in the former identifies these representatives with the prescribed finite twists. Consequently $Q_E$ is bounded constructible, has finite Tor amplitude (locally it is a shifted free module), and has a bounded-below etale-origin witness. The construction and source identification of $\tau_E$ are precisely [def-pur-vector-bundle-thom-class]. At $r=0$ that statement gives $E=B$, $\pi=z=1_B$ and $\tau_E=1_{A_B}$, proving this case. At $r=1$, (L1) of [thm-pur-localized-top-chern] identifies its supported class with the divisor class used in [thm-pur-rank-one-thom]. Thus the rank-one theorem concerns this specified map.

source.place: Opening sentence and Step 1: coefficient domains, rank-zero unit, and identification of the rank-one factors

proof.text:
Let $g:B'\to B$ be a change of base in the fixed setting, with $v:E'=E\times_BB'\to E$ and projection $\pi'$. The tautological section remains regular after this change of base, as stated in [def-pur-vector-bundle-thom-class]; (L2) of [thm-pur-localized-top-chern] therefore identifies the pulled-back supported morphism with $\operatorname{thom}(E')$. The exchange $C_{\pi,g}:g^{-1}R\pi_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi'_!v^{-1}$ is invertible on $Q_E$ by [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]. Its naturality applied to $\operatorname{thom}(E)$ gives a square between the compact images of the two supported maps. The square's source comparison, under $R\pi_!z_*A_B=A_B$, is the identity: paste the squares for $z$ and $\pi$, use $\pi z=1_B$, and use the identity and vertical-pasting normalization of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]. These are the etale exchanges whose transport defines the exchange in [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale]; [thm-sf-comp-composition] supplies the canonical source compositor and its identity normalization. With the twist pullback of Step 1 this yields the actual map equality
$$C_{\pi,g}(Q_E)\circ g^{-1}(\tau_E)=\tau_{E'}.$$
No flatness of $g$ is required: regularity here is the universal coordinate regularity of the tautological section, not regularity of an arbitrary pulled-back section.

source.place: Step 2, base change: naturality on the supported morphism and normalization of its source

proof.text:
Compute first for $V_j=\mathbf A^j_k$ over the fixed algebraically closed field $k$. Set $C_j=R\Gamma_c(V_j,A(j)[2j])$ and let $\tau_j:A\to C_j$ be the origin class. At the point, [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology] identifies the constant-section source with $A$. We prove by induction on $j$ that $\tau_j$ is invertible. Step 1 gives $j=0$ and the specified rank-one isomorphism $\tau_1$ from [thm-pur-rank-one-thom]. For $j\geq1$, write $V_{j+1}=V_j\times_kV_1$. The last clause of [def-pur-vector-bundle-thom-class] identifies the supported origin class with the cup product of the pulled-back classes. Apply [lem-pur-compact-product-proper-support-compatibility] to $X=V_j$, $Y=V_1$, $Z=W=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and coefficient twists $A(j),A(1)$. Its even-degree cup/exterior identification and its equation $u_{Z\times W}\kappa^{Z,W}=\kappa_c(u_Z\otimes u_W)$ give, after shifting,
$$\tau_{j+1}=\kappa_c\circ(\tau_j\otimes_A^L\tau_1).$$
The supports are points, hence proper, and the twist inputs satisfy its finite-Tor hypotheses by Step 1. The cited node says that this specified $\kappa_c$ is invertible. The inductive hypothesis and functoriality of tensor make the right side invertible, completing the induction. This verifies the image of the supported class, rather than merely computing the object $C_j$.

source.place: Step 1: iterated rank-one compact-support calculation, with the supported-to-compact map specified

proof.text: Choose a Zariski open cover of $B$ trivializing its locally free module, using [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] and the relative-Spec presentation of [def-pur-vector-bundle-zero-section]. The free symmetric-algebra isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-free-module-polynomial] identifies these bundle charts, including their augmentation zero sections, with $\mathbf A^r_U$. We may refine to principal affine opens in a finite-type affine cover of $B$; their rings are finitely generated $k$-algebras with one element inverted, still finitely generated by adjoining its inverse. Thus the charts remain in the fixed finite-type setting, and they are separated as open subschemes of $B$. On such a chart the bundle and its specified tautological class are pulled back from $V_r\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Step 2 identifies $\tau_{E|_U}$ with the pullback of the isomorphism $\tau_r$ from Step 3. It is therefore invertible. Clause 1 of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], applied to this Zariski (hence pro-etale) covering, now proves that the globally defined $\tau_E$ is invertible. This covering criterion is valid for the ordinary pro-etale derived category and does not assume geometric stalks detect all its sheaves. In particular $R\pi_!Q_E\cong A_B$ is concentrated in degree zero. The empty base is covered by the empty family and satisfies the same conclusion.

source.place: Steps 1 and 2: bundle charts and local detection of invertibility

proof.text:
Specify the direct-sum comparison. Let $\pi_i:E_i\to B$ have ranks $r_i$, put $Q_i=A_{E_i}(r_i)[2r_i]$, and identify $E=E_1\oplus E_2=E_1\times_BE_2$ and $Q_E=p_1^*Q_1\otimes_A^Lp_2^*Q_2$. Let
$$\kappa_B:R\pi_!Q_E\xrightarrow{\sim}R\pi_{1!}Q_1\otimes_A^LR\pi_{2!}Q_2$$
be the concrete relative Kunneth comparison of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative]. Its inputs are finite-Tor constructible by Step 1; Step 4 also identifies both individual compact images with $A_B$, so its projection-formula coefficient domains are satisfied. The same cited statement gives compatibility of this named map with base change. Its inverse is exactly the forward composite $T_{\pi_1,\pi_2}$ of [lem-pur-finite-product-compactification], since reversing the six displayed invertible arrows in the relative comparison gives that formula. For $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$, the latter node identifies $T$ on proper compactifications with the ordinary exterior-product map on extension-by-zero complexes. This is precisely the defining compact exterior product $\kappa_c$ of [lem-pur-compact-product-proper-support-compatibility], including its direction. Hence $\kappa_k^{-1}=\kappa_c$ with the specified coefficient and shift identifications.

source.place: Step 2, direct sums: specify the compact-support comparison rather than invoke an unnamed product

proof.text:
For the two trivial bundles $V_r,V_s$ over $k$, the supported class of $V_{r+s}=V_r\times_kV_s$ is the cup product of the two classes by (L3) of [thm-pur-localized-top-chern], equivalently by the last clause of [def-pur-vector-bundle-thom-class]. Transversality holds: the first $r$ and last $s$ independent coordinate equations remain regular after imposing either block, since the quotient is a polynomial ring in the remaining variables and multiplication by a remaining variable is injective by coefficient comparison. The supports in each factor are the origin points, proper over $k$. The same compatibility equation in [lem-pur-compact-product-proper-support-compatibility] used in Step 3, now for $V_r,V_s$, gives
$$\tau_{r+s}=\kappa_c(\tau_r\otimes_A^L\tau_s),\qquad \kappa_k\tau_{r+s}=\tau_r\otimes_A^L\tau_s.$$
Its cup/exterior clause applies because the degrees $2r,2s$ are even. If a rank is zero this is the tensor-unit identity, by the empty-product convention of [def-pur-vector-bundle-thom-class].

source.place: Step 2, direct sums: product of the two coordinate blocks on the universal trivial model

proof.text:
Trivialize $E_1$ and $E_2$ simultaneously on the intersections of their bundle charts from Step 4. On every such $U$ they and their direct sum are pulled back from $V_{r_1},V_{r_2},V_{r_1+r_2}$ over $k$. By Step 2 the three $\tau$ maps are the corresponding pullbacks; by the base-change clause of [sk-thm-sf-kunneth-relative] so is $\kappa_U$. Thus pulling back Step 6 proves, on every $U$,
$$\kappa_U\tau_{E|_U}=\tau_{E_1|_U}\otimes_A^L\tau_{E_2|_U}.$$
The two global maps in question have source $A_B$ (using $A_B\otimes_A^LA_B=A_B$) and target $R\pi_{1!}Q_1\otimes_A^LR\pi_{2!}Q_2$. By Step 4 that target is isomorphic to $A_B$, so source and target are concentrated in degree zero. Therefore [lem-pur-degree-zero-derived-map-gluing] applies to these two actual global maps and proves
$$\kappa_B\circ\tau_{E_1\oplus E_2}=\tau_{E_1}\otimes_A^L\tau_{E_2}.$$
This is the direct-sum compatibility asserted in the item. The equality is checked as a sheaf-map equality in degree zero, without any gluing or local detection assertion for arbitrary derived morphisms.

source.place: Step 2, direct sums: simultaneous charts and valid degree-zero equality detection

proof.text:
Define $\operatorname{tr}_\pi:=\tau_E^{-1}$, which exists uniquely by Step 4. Inverting the equation of Step 2 proves its base-change compatibility. Inverting the equation of Step 7 gives
$$\operatorname{tr}_{\pi_1\oplus\pi_2}=(\operatorname{tr}_{\pi_1}\otimes_A^L\operatorname{tr}_{\pi_2})\circ\kappa_B.$$
At rank zero this is the identity. These are consequences of uniqueness of inverses and tensor functoriality, and give the displayed trace with its specified normalization.

source.place: Statement, final display: inverse trace and inherited compatibilities
